items.title: The total localized Chern class of a direct sum is the product of the total classes of the summands

items.difficulty_reason: In the setting of Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre the lemma assumes that Q|_T is finite locally free of rank < p, takes a second perfect object Q' whose Chern classes are defined with Q'|_T finite locally free of rank < p' in cohomological degree 0, and with the truncated total classes c^{(p)}(Q) of Remark labelled remark-ring-loc-classes asserts c^{(p + p')}(Q oplus Q') = c^{(p)}(Q) c^{(p')}(Q') in A^{(p + p')}(Z -> X) (statement lines 10498-10517). The proof first disposes of the degrees below p + p': the image of c'_i(Q) in A^p(X) is c_i(Q|_{X x {0}}) by Lemma labelled lemma-localized-chern-pre, so those degrees follow from the additivity stated in Lemma labelled lemma-additivity-on-perfect (proof lines 10519-10527). For degrees at least p + p' it writes E for the inverse image of Z in W_infinity, invokes the equality c^{(p + p')}(Q|_E oplus Q'|_E) = c^{(p)}(Q|_E) c^{(p')}(Q'|_E) of Lemma labelled lemma-silly-sum-c, and uses the description c'_p(Q oplus Q') = (E -> Z)_* o c'_p(Q|_E oplus Q'|_E) o C to reduce to the identity (E -> Z)_* o c^{(p)}_i(Q|_E) c^{(p')}_j(Q'|_E) o C = c^{(p)}_i(Q) c^{(p')}_j(Q') for i + j = n (proof lines 10529-10547). It then splits into the three position cases i >= p and j >= p', i >= p and j < p, and i < p and j >= p', which are settled by Lemma labelled lemma-silly, the second part of Lemma labelled lemma-homomorphism and the commutation of capping with bivariant Chern classes in Lemma labelled lemma-cap-commutative-chern respectively (proof lines 10549-10600). Matching the two different products on the localized classes through the three cases and the insertion of the pushforwards is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
